finding.claim: SQL injection in /search: the unauthenticated query parameter `q` is interpolated directly into the SQL string with an f-string. An attacker can break out of the LIKE literal and run UNION-based queries to read any table in shop.db. The sqlite3 driver is also reachable for stacked-query-style abuse only via execute() limits, so the main impact is data exfiltration and boolean/blind extraction.
finding.sink: db.execute(f"SELECT id, name FROM products WHERE name LIKE '%{term}%'") at app.py:12, result returned as JSON at app.py:13

trace.note: Public Flask route /search registered with no auth decorator
term = request.args.get('q','') takes attacker-controlled input, no validation or escaping
term is formatted into the SQL text via f-string and executed
Query results are returned to the attacker via jsonify, so UNION SELECT output is directly visible

finding.guards_checked: No parameterization (the other routes at app.py:18 and :25 use ? placeholders, this one does not). No input validation, allowlist, escaping, WAF or auth middleware. Flask has no implicit SQL protection. Route is public ingress with framework defaults.

verdict.reason: app.py:11-12 takes request.args['q'] and f-string-interpolates it into a LIKE query on a public route with no auth decorator (app.py:9), and app.py:13 returns the rows via jsonify, so UNION-based extraction works; only the other routes (app.py:18, :25) use ? placeholders.
